$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under src/ imports this file.
purpose: The guard ledger for WIN-258 TRANCHE 5 — `observability`'s canonical store, the
THIRTEENTH owner behind the one PostgreSQL client ADR M0.3 §15 gives the ORM.
One entry per guard: per scope clause that stands where no ancestry rule
stands, per shape check that stands where a migration-only CHECK stands, per
refusal code that has to stay distinguishable from its neighbour, and per
statement the port's contract says must be sent rather than anticipated.
Each carries the file it lives in, the EXACT text that implements it
(`from`), the edit that removes it (`to`), and the NAMED cases that were seen
to go red (`kills`).
IT IS A THIRTEENTH FILE beside mutations.json, mutations-identity.json,
mutations-ports.json, mutations-outbox.json, mutations-tools.json,
mutations-agents.json, mutations-cost.json, mutations-channels.json,
mutations-governance.json, mutations-secrets.json, mutations-providers.json,
mutations-conversations.json, mutations-skills.json and mutations-memory.json
rather than an extension of any of them, for the reason the fourth was:
separate tranches are separate claims about separate port surfaces, and a
reader checking one should not have to read past the others. All are hashed
by the same packages.adapters.config rule and counted together by the v1
ledger.
WHY THIS TRANCHE NEEDED ITS OWN SWEEP, AND WHAT IT FOUND.
`AdminAudit` IS APPEND-ONLY IN THE DATABASE AND THE PORT ASKS FOR AN UPDATE.
`00000000000000_initial/migration.sql` installs `reject_admin_audit_mutation()`
on UPDATE, on DELETE and on TRUNCATE and withdraws all three privileges from
PUBLIC. `ObservabilityRepository.clearAdminAuditActor` is defined as an UPDATE
returning rows changed, so against a database these migrations build it can
return zero or refuse and nothing else — and the context's own in-memory
double unlinks happily, which is trap 2 of this issue in its second form: the
double does not mint a value the database refuses, it performs an OPERATION
the database refuses. M-O17, M-O13, M-O14 and M-O24 are the four halves of
keeping that refusal visible, distinguishable from an outage, and NOT
anticipated by this package.
AND THE TABLE HAS NO ANCESTRY RULE WHILE THE RECORD HAS A THREE-LEVEL SCOPE.
`AdminAudit` is not among the thirty-eight tables carrying
`enforce_domain_ancestry`, and it stores ONE scope column. So the containment
an `EnvironmentScope` asserts is this adapter's WHERE clause or nobody's, and
the three clauses have to be told APART rather than proved as a group: a
foreign tenant fails all three at once. M-O02 needs a SIBLING ENVIRONMENT
under the same project, M-O03 a SIBLING PROJECT under the same organization,
and M-O16 a scope that keeps the right project and lies about the
organization. Two of those three fixtures exist only for the sweep.
ONE ENTRY IS HONESTLY WEAKER THAN THE REST AND SAYS SO. M-O04 removes the
organization clause from the READ predicate, and no integration case can see
it: `Project.organizationId` is a column, so a row whose project matches
necessarily has a matching organization, and the read's project clause
implies the one M-O04 removes. It is killed by the shape case in
`observability-rows.test.ts` and it is defence in depth on the read path —
which is not the same as being untested, and is not the same as being
load-bearing either. The WRITE path's organization clause IS load-bearing and
is M-O16, because there the environment is named directly and its project is
not.
procedure: PROVE THE SUITES GREEN FIRST. Tranche 1's first sweep reported 22 kills and
every one was VACUOUS: a context's `dist` had been cleaned, so every suite
failed to load its import and would have 'died' against any mutation at all,
including none. The driver runs each suite set UNMUTATED and refuses to
sweep unless it is green with a non-zero executed case count, and classifies
a run with no executed cases as VACUOUS rather than as a kill.
THE INTEGRATION SUITES RUN ON A REAL POSTGRESQL, in a container, on the
machine that has a daemon. `observability-rows.test.ts` is the only suite
here that runs without one, and it is the one that reaches the mapping
branches a container suite cannot: a container only ever reads rows THIS
binary wrote, so the non-object-snapshot branch is unreachable from it except
through the two rows the constraints suite plants as raw SQL.
EVERY `from` IS A UNIQUE SUBSTRING OF ITS FILE and is applied literally, so a
mutation that no longer matches is a LEDGER FAULT rather than a silent skip.
The driver rebuilds the package between mutations, because
`pnpm test:v1-foundation` runs `test:clean-v1` and a sweep over a cleaned
`dist` reproduces exactly the vacuity above.
TWO ENTRIES ARE SPELLED SO THE COMPILER DOES NOT KILL THEM FIRST, and that
is a property of the sweep rather than a courtesy to the mutation. M-O06's
first spelling compared a `JsonObject | undefined` to `null` and M-O24's
removed the only use of an import; both failed `tsc` before a single case
ran, and a mutation the BUILD refuses says nothing about whether a SUITE
would have caught it. Each is now an edit that compiles and changes
behaviour, so the kill is a red case rather than a red compiler.
THREE ENTRIES BELOW WERE WRITTEN AFTER A SURVIVOR RATHER THAN BEFORE ONE.
M-O02 survived its first sweep because the only cross-tenant fixture was a
second ORGANIZATION, which fails the project and organization clauses too —
so removing the environment clause changed no observation. M-O03 and M-O16
survived for the mirror-image reason on the write path. Each is now a named
case with a fixture built for it: `siblingEnvironment` and `siblingProject`
in `observability-harness.ts` exist for no other purpose.

mutations.name: M-O01 rows: a row outside the proven scope is refused, not relabelled
mutations.note: The record's scope is the one the predicate proved, so the row is never asked for its ancestry. This is the backstop that stops a widened predicate RELABELLING a sibling environment's rows with the caller's scope instead of failing.
kills: the scope a row does not carry a row from a DIFFERENT environment is refused rather than relabelled

mutations.name: M-O02 rows: the read predicate names the ENVIRONMENT
mutations.note: A sibling environment under the same project satisfies BOTH relation clauses, so without this one a trail read returns the sibling's rows. It is the only clause a second ORGANIZATION cannot test, which is why `siblingEnvironment` exists.
kills: a SIBLING environment under the same project is excluded, which only the environment clause can do
the scope a row does not carry an environment read names all THREE levels, so a mismatched scope matches nothing

mutations.name: M-O03 rows: the read predicate names the PROJECT
mutations.note: Without it a read scoped to one project returns another project's environment when the caller passes its id — and the record comes back wearing the caller's project.

The WRITE path's organization clause is a different guard and IS load-bearing — see M-O16.

mutations.name: M-O17 audit: the unlink statement is SENT rather than anticipated
mutations.to:
actorUserId: selector.actorUserId,
            ...organizationWhere(selector.organizationId),
            id: "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000",
          },
          data: { actorUserId: null },
mutations.note: THE ENTRY THAT KEEPS THE FINDING NON-VACUOUS. Narrowed to match nothing, the unlink returns `ok(0)` and every claim about the append-only rule becomes unfalsifiable — the refusal would look identical to a port that quietly did nothing. This is why `observability-audit.ts` sends a statement it knows will raise instead of refusing from memory.
